Medicare Part D is integral to our seniors' care.

It keeps costs low & ensures they have reliable, affordable access to the drugs they need. In the #IncomeReductionAct, changes to Part D will CUT drug benefits - meaning their premiums & out-of-pocket expenses will skyrocket.
These drug pricing controls are not going to help the people who need it most - our seniors. The Democrats' plan will hinder American innovation and leave our Medicare patients in the dust.

Competition in the free market is the only way to lower prices and incentivize innovation. Government price controls won't help - in fact, they'll make your premiums go up.

Yesterday, I discovered the federal Dept. of Health and Human Services arbitrarily asked St. Francis Hospital in Tulsa to extinguish their eternal flame, calling it a safety hazard.

I am enraged at this blatant disregard for religious liberty and federal government overreach.

Was the federal department of Health and Human Services trying to keep patients safe from a small, and ENCLOSED eternal flame? 

Or were they using any excuse in the books to punish an organization that proudly serves God and the people of their community?

Federal officials told St. Francis that open flames aren’t allowed in a patient's room or near medical equipment.
 
But here’s the thing: the flame was in a sanctuary, nowhere near any patient’s room or near any medical equipment.

From @CharlieKatebi of @AFPhq:
If you see your doctor for a checkup you shouldn’t pay for a hospital visit.

Patients and families deserve a Personal Option in health care that puts an end to dishonest billing and surprise unexpected costs.

From @Josselinsweet of @NFIB:
We applaud Hern and Kuster's commitment to providing relief to small businesses and their employees by: 
- Addressing the underlying cost drivers of health insurance 
- Increasing healthcare transparency and competition in the market.

From @benefitscouncil:
The trajectory of health care costs is unsustainable. And it's only exacerbated by opaque billing practices.

We must shine a light on disparities in cost of care at hospital and non-hospital settings – and extend this transparency to private sector plans.

From @JamesGelfand of @ERISAIndCmte:
The FAIR Act, by addressing a commonsense billing issue, will increase much needed transparency and lead to significant savings overall for taxpayers, employers, unions, and patients.

ERIC strongly supports this bill.

From @HealthCareFight:
Patients should not have to pay more simply because a hospital buys a doctor’s office & engages in billing practices that obscure the location of care. 

The FAIR Act injects transparency into hospital billing to ensure patients pay for service provided.

From @AlexSchriver of @bettersol4hc:
This measure will end dishonest hospital billing and lower prices for employers and consumers by ensuring that patients are billed for the services they receive at the location where they receive them.

From @BCBSAssociation:
No one should have to pay more for health care services based only on the location of care. 

This bipartisan, commonsense solution prioritizes the health and well-being of patients by promoting affordability, transparency and fairness.

RIGHT NOW: Our taxpayer dollars are going to the World Health Organization. 

Yes, the same WHO that refused to hold China accountable for the loss of more than a million Americans and thousands of Oklahomans due to COVID-19.

It's time to LEAVE the globalist WHO!

The cost of healthcare, and the ever-growing burden of paperwork, has become a massive hardship for both employers and employees. 

My bill puts employees in the driver’s seat when it comes to picking their health care plan, and lets employers financially support their decision.

Prescription digital therapeutics (PDTs) use the latest technology to help patients improve their health.

I introduced the Access to PDTs Act to increase the number of patients who can benefit from them!

Recently, I was able to test several PDTs. Thanks, @amcporg, for hosting! https://t.co/Hqs8u8LAKi

How do we cut healthcare costs WITHOUT hurting access or quality? 🤔

By ENDING dishonest billing.

That's when a hospital secretly reclassifies an off-site doctor’s office as a hospital & charges up to 10X the normal amount.

I introduced a bill w/ @RepAnnieKuster to fight back.

The Washington Examiner just published my in-depth analysis of rising healthcare costs, and the importance of ending dishonest billing.

READ MORE in the @dcexaminer: https://t.co/oqhN7yeQfr

A recent report shows the amount of CHOICE account users increased by 171% over the last year. 

These are reimbursement accounts that allow employees to use money from their employer to shop for their own healthcare coverage (they’re also known as ICHRAs).
